title: Where it stands, 22 October
subtitle: The situation at the latest capture, 11:34 UTC on 22 October 2026, for someone who runs a website. 10 panels.
rule: Every line a character says is the storyboard's own words, not a quote, and is marked not_a_quote; every evidence panel quotes this site's data word for word and names the file (quote_from), which the gate checks; every panel cites the evidence vault's source slugs it rests on (cites), which the gate checks against the manifest.

scenes.title: Where it stands
scenes.subtitle: Two PHP flaws, one fix, 22 October 2026, 11:34 UTC
scenes.note: Who this is for: Casey, who runs a website on PHP and heard about it on the news.

scenes.caption: The question

cast.says: The radio says websites are going offline. Is mine?
Let me show you what is confirmed first.

scenes.note: The headlines on the morning of 22 October: sites dark, governments warning.

scenes.caption: What happened

evidence.quote: Either lets anyone on the internet, with no password, run commands on the web server.

scenes.note: Two flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both 9.2 out of 10, both in PHP itself.

scenes.caption: Where the hole is
scenes.note: Not your phone or laptop: the flaw is on web servers. Visitors are affected only indirectly.

scenes.caption: The fix, since 21 October

cast.says: Four fixed versions. Updated AND restarted.

scenes.note: The fix is in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, released on 21 October 2026. Websites on PHP 8.1 or older have no ready-made fix.

scenes.caption: Attackers are trying
scenes.note: Attempts reported by one CDN in the millions by 01:25 UTC on 22 October; Amazon reports a honeypot hit on 17 October. Attempts are requests, not break-ins.

scenes.caption: Has anyone been hacked?

evidence.quote: Attackers are trying to use the flaws, in large numbers. No organisation has said it was broken into.

scenes.note: CISA's list of flaws known to be used in attacks did not include either one at the latest capture.

scenes.caption: How sure is this site?
scenes.note: Counted from every claim on /claims/; confirmed means two or more original sources agree.

scenes.caption: What nobody knows yet
scenes.note: The five open questions on the front page, each updated when the evidence is.

scenes.punchline: Update PHP. Restart it. Ask your host to confirm both.
scenes.note: What should be done, from the PHP project and the agencies: the fixed version, restarted; if not today, the temporary settings, a firewall in front, and offline as a last resort.
